scene: Home living room evening, two dogs playing with ONE soft hollow mesh-like rubber ball (open lattice sphere, not tennis felt; teal or muted orange). Buddy has just tried to trap it by lying on it but missed: now landed on his SIDE on rug, one continuous full torso supported on hip/shoulder, four relaxed/folded legs owned naturally, head lifted toward ball rolling a short distance beyond his paws. Neet stands eagerly nearby on all four fine legs watching escaped ball, ready to follow. No ball under or fused through Buddy body. A couple sofa cushions displaced behind but no chaotic clutter. Comedy is earnest bodily trapping plan versus bouncy toy. Full drawn anatomy/ground contacts, no motion streaks. Smooth close dog coats with regional Buddy face and ears only.
placement_after: Neet was doing parkour off the furniture. Buddy tried to trap the ball by lying on top of it. When it slipped away, he landed on his side, got up and tried again from the opposite direction.
alt_text: The hollow mesh ball escapes Buddy’s attempted body trap as Neet waits eagerly to chase it.
